title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup
book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Stage 2 Reclaim, VCP Squeeze & Ratcheted Stop

epigraph.quote: Respect a confirmed Stage 2 reclaim on existing shares by ratcheting your stop higher—never by chasing a thin-volume bounce with fresh capital when reward-to-risk is below 1-to-1.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein & Multi-Timeframe Desk

summary: Following the Nov 18–19 GlobalFoundries catalyst, Cyient upgraded from Stage 3 back to confirmed STAGE_2 (Markup) on both the 23 November 2026 NSE ledger (₹1,160.50) and the 25 November 2026 live TradingView snapshot (₹1,151.20, +2.27% vs 10W EMA, +2.51% vs 50D SMA, 8.57% VCP squeeze, 4H turn confirmed). However, live volume is thin (0.24x 30D avg) and CMP R:R is inverted (0.88:1). We ratchet the structural stop upward from ₹951.20 to ₹970.95 (live TV stop). CYIENT remains NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID (not in NSE F&O).

web_blocks.html: Price action improved sharply since our 13 November audit, driven by GlobalFoundries' 18–19 November $10M CCPS deal [10][28]. On the verified 23 November 2026 NSE ledger, Cyient closed at ₹1,160.50 (+0.43% 1D, +5.19% 1W, +28.51% 3M) [34]. It upgraded from Stage 3 to Stage 2 (Markup) above its rising 50-day SMA (₹1,120.33) and 20-day SMA (₹1,129.09). Ledger metrics show 3 distribution days, +23.90% 63-day RS, and -12.77% 28-day RS [34].

On the 25 November 2026 live TradingView snapshot, shares trade at ₹1,151.20 (-0.80% 1D, +6.52% 1W), 9.85% off the ₹1,277.00 high [28]. The technical gate reads STAGE_2 / CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION. Price sits +2.27% above the 10-week EMA (₹1,125.60), +2.51% above the 50-day SMA (₹1,122.96), and +15.96% above the rising 30-week SMA (₹992.74) [28]. Bollinger bandwidth squeezed to 8.57% (STAGE2_VCP_VOLATILITY_SQUEEZE) and the 4H chart turned up (above 4H EMA20 ₹1,126.83 and SMA50 ₹1,137.03) [28]. Yet volume stayed thin at 286,790 shares (0.24x 30D avg). That signals a quiet coil, not an institutional breakout [28].

web_blocks.takeaway: Technically, Cyient is a clean Stage 2 VCP squeeze with a confirmed 4H turn—justifying holding existing shares with a higher ₹970.95 stop—but thin 0.24x volume and a 15.66% stop distance make chasing ₹1,151.20 mathematically inferior to waiting for ₹1,043–₹1,095.

web_blocks.html: Upward-Only Stop-Loss Ratchet: The rising 30-week SMA climbed from ₹974.01 (13 Nov) to ₹992.74 (25 Nov) [28]. Live TradingView invalidation support stepped up from ₹951.20 to ₹970.95 [28]. Following our upward-only ratchet rule, we raise the hard exit stop on our 92 Zerodha shares from ₹951.20 to ₹970.95 (+₹19.75). This floor sits ~2.2% below the 30-week SMA and just above the 200-day SMA (₹964.11) [28][34].

Domestic Institutional Investors anchor the float at 38.96% (Sep 2026), up from 22.69% in Dec 2023 [1]. DIIs absorbed a two-year FII exit (34.11% down to 14.72%, ticking +0.20% QoQ in Q2 FY27), while promoter stake rose to 24.75% post-buyback [1]. Options verification confirms CYIENT is not in the NSE F&O segment (NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID). All exposure stays strictly in cash equity [33].

Broader Indian market breadth reinforces patience. On the 23 November 2026 ledger, Nifty 50 sits in an Uptrend (narrow breadth) [34]. Only 55.2% of the 500-stock pool trades above its 50-DMA (down from 72.1% on 13 Nov), and 48.2% above its 200-DMA, with 7 of 11 sectors healthy and 3 distribution days [34]. In narrow breadth, thin-volume VCP coils often retest Pivot S1 / 200D EMA (₹1,042–₹1,095) before advancing [28][34].

book_paragraphs: In Chapter 7, we saw that Cyient at ₹1,151.20 on the 25 November live TradingView screen (₹1,160.50 on the 23 November NSE ledger) offers only +13.8% upside to our honest, earnout-adjusted ₹1,310.00 Base Case target. Now let us turn to Chapter 8 and read the price tape—because the tape just delivered a major technical upgrade that we must respect without losing our valuation discipline.

Between our prior November 13 audit and today, one event flipped the chart: GlobalFoundries' November 18–19 announcement of a $10 million strategic CCPS investment in Cyient Semiconductors at a $510 million post-money valuation. That news propelled Cyient back above its 50-day moving average and upgraded the stock from Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) back into a confirmed Stan Weinstein Stage 2 (Markup) uptrend on BOTH our verified 23 November 2026 NSE ledger (₹1,160.50, +5.19% 1W, +28.51% 3M) and our live 25 November 2026 TradingView snapshot (₹1,151.20, +6.52% 1W, +10.16% 3M).

Look closely at how constructive the multi-timeframe structure has become. On the weekly chart, Cyient sits +15.96% above its rising 30-week Simple Moving Average (which climbed from ₹974.01 on November 13 to ₹992.74 on November 25) and +2.27% above its 10-week Exponential Moving Average (₹1,125.60), with weekly RSI at 60.54. On the daily chart, price sits +2.51% above its rising 50-day SMA (₹1,122.96 TV; ₹1,120.33 ledger), +2.60% above its 20-day SMA (₹1,121.99), and +19.41% above its 200-day SMA (₹964.11), with daily RSI at a balanced 55.43. Even better, Bollinger bandwidth has tightened to 8.57%—a textbook Volatility Contraction Pattern (VCP) squeeze—and the 4-hour chart has flipped cleanly bullish (intraday_4h_turn: true), with price above both its 4-hour 20-EMA (₹1,126.83) and 4-hour 50-SMA (₹1,137.03) and 4-hour RSI at 56.52.

So why aren't we rushing to hit the buy button with fresh cash? Two technical clues—plus one hard mathematical reality. First, look at volume: Cyient traded just 286,790 shares on the live 25 November snapshot against a 30-day average of 1,185,388 shares (0.24x), matching the 0.25x relative volume (391,552 shares) on the 23 November ledger. That is a quiet coil, not an institutional volume surge breaking out past Pivot R1 (₹1,251.93). Second, look at the broader Indian market regime on our 23 November ledger: Nifty 50 remains in an Uptrend (narrow breadth), where the share of 500 tracked stocks above their 50-day moving average has narrowed from 72.1% on November 13 down to just 55.2% (and only 48.2% above their 200-day moving average), with 3 distribution days. Narrow-breadth regimes are notorious for false thin-volume breakouts that retest deeper support.

Now pair those technical clues with our upward-only stop-loss ratchet. Because the 30-week SMA climbed to ₹992.74, TradingView's structural invalidation stop stepped up from ₹951.20 to ₹970.95—an upward ratchet of +₹19.75 (+2.08%) that we immediately adopt to protect our existing 92 Zerodha shares. Yet from ₹1,151.20 down to ₹970.95 is a -15.66% stop distance (₹180.25 of risk per share), while upside to our ₹1,310.00 Base Case target is only ₹158.80 (+13.79%). That gives a fresh buyer at CMP an inverted 0.88-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio (0.79-to-1 at the ₹1,160.50 ledger close). Even TradingView's near-term support band (₹1,108.72–₹1,143.83) only yields 0.96-to-1 to 1.46-to-1—still shy of our 1.50-to-1 minimum hurdle.

By contrast, look down to the next structural demand shelf on the chart: Pivot S1 at ₹1,042.93, the 200-day EMA at ₹1,041.93, and the 20-day swing low at ₹1,065.80 (just below the 50-day EMA at ₹1,105.79). Defining our disciplined fresh-capital entry zone at ₹1,043.00–₹1,095.00 shrinks downside risk to ₹72.05–₹124.05 while lifting upside to ₹215.00–₹267.00—delivering a clean 1.73-to-1 to 3.71-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio. Remember also that Cyient is not listed in the NSE F&O segment (NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID), so cash-equity entry price and our ratcheted ₹970.95 stop are our sole risk-management levers.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION — When Technicals Say 'Clear' but Valuation Says 'Wait'
book_callouts.text: The automated Stage 2 scanner evaluates trend health and non-extension—and rightly upgrades Cyient to STAGE_2 / CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION. But an automated screen never reads Footnote 14 on ₹926.80 crore of TAO Digital earnouts or enforces a 1.50:1 fundamental R:R hurdle. Letting the tape protect your held shares via a higher ₹970.95 stop while letting valuation govern fresh cash is how institutions avoid overpaying for good news.

book_subsections.title: Walking the Three Timeframes: Weekly VCP Coil vs. Narrow-Breadth Reality
paragraphs: Let us walk through Cyient's 25 November 2026 chart from top to bottom—Weekly, Daily, and 4-Hour—so you can see every shelf with complete clarity. On the Weekly timeframe, the primary trend is firmly restored. Cyient trades at ₹1,151.20 (+15.96% above its rising 30-week SMA of ₹992.74 and +2.27% above its 10-week EMA of ₹1,125.60), carrying a bullish weekly RSI of 60.54 and a TheWrap RS percentile of 80.1 (though Packaged Software sector Stage 2 density sits at a modest 30.8%, rank 44). That weekly posture confirms that institutional buyers defended the November pullback and rewarded the GlobalFoundries announcement.

On the Daily chart, the stock has formed a remarkably tight volatility contraction. Bollinger bandwidth narrowed to just 8.57% as price coiled above the 20-day SMA (₹1,121.99), 50-day SMA (₹1,122.96), and 50-day EMA (₹1,105.79). The 23 November NSE ledger confirms the same structure: SMA50 at ₹1,120.33 is officially RISING, 63-day relative strength is +23.90% (though 28-day RS is still -12.77% from the October consolidation), and ATR14 is ₹44.27 (₹43.58 on live TV). Yet daily volume has dried up to 0.24x–0.25x average. In Mark Minervini and Stan Weinstein's playbook, volume dry-up inside a tight VCP is constructive setup behavior—but you only trust a breakout when volume expands to at least 1.5x average (above 1.8 million shares) as price clears Pivot R1 (₹1,251.93) and the 52-week high (₹1,277.00).

On the 4-Hour chart, short-term momentum has clearly repaired itself compared to November 13. Price (₹1,151.20) now sits above both the 4-hour 20-period EMA (₹1,126.83) and the 4-hour 50-period SMA (₹1,137.03), with 4-hour RSI at 56.52. That removes the immediate falling-knife risk we saw two weeks ago—which is great news for our 92 held shares—even though it does not fix the inverted 0.88:1 fundamental reward-to-risk ratio for fresh capital.

book_subsections.title: Exact Price Shelves, Institutional Float & Cash-Equity Stop Discipline
paragraphs: Map the exact battleground levels on your TradingView screen. Overhead, Pivot Middle sits right at ₹1,159.97 (almost identical to the 23 November ledger close of ₹1,160.50), followed by Pivot R1 at ₹1,251.93, the 52-week high at ₹1,277.00, and our Base Case fair value at ₹1,310.00. Below current price, short-term moving-average support clusters around ₹1,105.79–₹1,126.93 (50-day EMA to 20-day EMA). Beneath that sits our true value-and-technical confluence zone: ₹1,043.00–₹1,095.00, anchored by the 20-day swing low (₹1,065.80), Pivot S1 (₹1,042.93), and the 200-day EMA (₹1,041.93).

Below ₹1,042 lies the structural floor: the rising 30-week SMA at ₹992.74, our newly ratcheted hard invalidation stop at ₹970.95, the 200-day SMA at ₹964.11, and Pivot S2 at ₹950.97. Ratcheting our stop upward from ₹951.20 to ₹970.95 respects the rising 30-week average while giving the position roughly 3.5x–4.1x daily ATR breathing room from current levels so normal day-to-day noise will not shake us out prematurely.

Underneath the chart, the institutional float remains tightly held. DIIs own 38.96% as of September 2026 (up from 22.69% in December 2023), FIIs stabilized at 14.72% (+0.20 percentage points QoQ), promoters hold 24.75% following the July 2026 tender-offer buyback, and total retail shareholders declined from 2,61,505 to 1,99,848. Because Cyient is excluded from the NSE F&O segment—meaning zero listed puts or call spreads exist to hedge balance-sheet or earnings surprises—that tighter float cuts both ways: it amplifies upside squeezes on good news like GlobalFoundries, and amplifies air pockets if Q3 FY27 debt or Semiconductor losses disappoint. Disciplined cash-equity sizing and our ₹970.95 hard stop are non-negotiable.
